value: Study population: 77 females with anorexia nervosa (AN) and 70 healthy female controls (HC)
Study design: Cross-sectional observational study with mechanistic animal model component
Study sites: Three specialized eating disorder centres in Denmark (Odense University Hospital, Aarhus University Hospital, Aalborg University Hospital)
Animal model: Female germ-free Swiss Webster mice (3 AN donors, 3 HC donors; 10 AN-T and 10 HC-T recipients)
AN subtypes: AN-restricting (AN-RS) n=56, AN-binge/purging (AN-BP) n=21
Faecal microbiota transplantation (FMT) was performed under 30% energy-restricted diet for 3 weeks
uncurated_metadata.evidence_quote: 77 females with AN and 70 healthy females...recruited from three specialized centres in Denmark from 1 September 2014 to 31 July 2016

study_name.notes: No canonical study name identifier (e.g., EinsteinA_YYYY format) is provided in the paper. The study is identified by ClinicalTrials.gov NCT02217384.

curator.notes: No curator information is provided in the paper.

target_condition.evidence_quote: The gut microbiota contributes to the pathogenesis of anorexia nervosa in humans and mice
target_condition.notes: Primary phenotype is anorexia nervosa (AN), including both restricting (AN-RS) and binge-eating/purging (AN-BP) subtypes.

antibiotics_exclusion_period.evidence_quote: Exclusion criteria comprised antibiotic or antifungal treatment within the previous 3 months

antibiotics_exclusion_period_unit.evidence_quote: Exclusion criteria comprised antibiotic or antifungal treatment within the previous 3 months

dna_extraction_kit.evidence_quote: Microbial DNAs were isolated and purified from stool samples using NucleoSpin soil mini kit (MACHEREY‑NAGEL)
dna_extraction_kit.section: Methods — DNA extraction, 16S rRNA sequencing and data analyses in mice experiments
dna_extraction_kit.notes: For human faecal samples in the main analyses, the paper states DNA extraction was 'performed following IHMS SOP P7 V2' but does not name a specific kit. The NucleoSpin soil mini kit was used in the mouse experiments.

sequencing_platform.evidence_quote: Purified and amplified DNA fragment libraries were sequenced using the Ion Proton Sequencer (Thermo Fisher)
sequencing_platform.notes: Ion Proton Sequencer is the instrument name; 'Ion Torrent Proton' is the platform designation. For 16S rRNA sequencing in mice, Illumina MiSeq was used.

host_species.evidence_quote: 77 females with AN and 70 healthy females...faecal microbiota transplantation...to female germ-free littermates
host_species.notes: Study includes both human participants (primary analysis) and mouse recipients of faecal microbiota transplantation (mechanistic validation).

extraction_warnings: Granularity set to sample_level because two distinct cohorts (AN cases and HC controls) are described, but per-individual sample IDs and subject IDs are not provided in the paper. The extraction represents cohort-level metadata for two cohort groups rather than true per-sample rows.

The paper reports n=77 females with AN and n=70 healthy control females but does not provide individual subject or sample identifiers in the main text or supplementary tables accessible in the provided content.
Age is reported as 'age-matched' but no specific age values are given for the human cohorts in the main text. Age groups and min/max are inferred from DSM-5 criteria and 'female' classification.

BMI values are not provided for individual participants; the paper states AN cases 'were much leaner' and controls had 'healthy weight' (BMI 18.5–25 kg/m²) but no specific per-sample values are listed.
Ancestry reported as 'Danish Caucasian women' in Methods section.

Antibiotics exclusion criterion: 'Exclusion criteria comprised antibiotic or antifungal treatment within the previous 3 months'; controls had 'antibiotics within the last 3 months' as exclusion criterion—coded as 'No' current use.
Disease field for AN cases inferred from diagnostic criteria (DSM-5 restricting or binge/purging subtypes); controls classified as 'Healthy'.
Batch 1 returned granularity='subgroup_level', differs from batch 0 ('sample_level'); kept batch 0.

Batch 1 subgroups ['Anorexia Nervosa (AN)', 'Healthy Controls (HC)', 'AN-Restricting Subtype (AN-RS)', 'AN-Binge/Purging Subtype (AN-BP)', 'FMT AN-Transplanted Mice (AN-T)', 'FMT HC-Transplanted Mice (HC-T)'] differ from batch 0 []; kept batch 0.

The paper is primarily a cohort study with two groups (AN and HC) and does not report per-sample clinical phenotype data in a table format suitable for sample-level extraction. Granularity is subgroup_level.
Many biomarker values are referenced in Supplementary Tables (1 and 2) but specific numerical values are not reproduced in the main text extraction.

The FMT experiment involved 3 human donors and their littermate mouse recipients across 3 independent litters, but no detailed individual-level phenotype data for each mouse recipient is provided; only aggregate statistics.
Birth control use is mentioned only as an exclusion criterion for healthy controls, not as a measured variable.
Smoking status was adjusted for in analyses but individual participant smoking status is not reported.
No overall survival, RECIST response, PFS, or other oncology-relevant endpoints apply to this eating disorder study.
HLA typing, neonatal parameters, and tumor staging are not applicable to this study population.
Batch 2 returned granularity='study_level', differs from batch 0 ('sample_level'); kept batch 0.

The schema field 'dna_extraction_kit' requests a single enum value but the paper uses different kits for human (IHMS SOP P7 V2, not specifically named) versus mouse (NucleoSpin soil mini kit) samples. Returned the mouse kit value; human extraction method is not explicitly named as a commercial kit.

The schema field 'sequencing_platform' requests a single value but the paper uses two platforms: Ion Proton Sequencer (for shotgun metagenomics of human faecal DNA) and Illumina MiSeq (for 16S rRNA amplicon sequencing of mouse samples). Returned Ion Proton as the primary metagenomic platform used for the main human analyses.
The field 'host_species' allows enum values 'Human' or 'Mouse' but this study includes both. Returned as a list containing both values to reflect the dual-species design.
The 'study_name' field expects a canonical identifier (e.g., EinsteinA_YYYY) but the paper provides only a ClinicalTrials.gov registry number (NCT02217384). No formatted study name is reported.
